recognize_zh: 網狀纖維銀染（reticulin stain）下，黑色纖維粗厚、呈束狀平行流線並大量交錯，遠超過正常稀疏細纖維，並夾雜黃褐色含鐵血黃素顆粒，代表明顯網狀纖維增生。
features: Coarse, thick black argyrophilic fibers in streaming parallel bundles
Extensive fiber intersections with focal dense clumps
Pale green-counterstained residual cells entrapped between fibers
Scattered yellow-brown refractile pigment clumps (hemosiderin in macrophages)
Diffuse increase rather than focal perivascular distribution
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy stained for reticulin (silver impregnation with light green counterstain) shows a diffuse, dense increase in coarse, thick reticulin fibers arranged in streaming bundles with extensive intersections. Residual marrow cells are entrapped between fibers, and scattered yellow-brown pigmented macrophages consistent with hemosiderin are seen. The fiber density corresponds to a high-grade reticulin fibrosis (approximately MF-2 to MF-3; confirmation of collagen requires trichrome). Findings are consistent with marked marrow fibrosis; etiology requires correlation with H&E morphology and clinical findings.

ddx.vs: Normal marrow shows only scattered fine linear fibers without intersections, mostly around vessels, unlike the coarse dense bundles here.
PMF is favored when the fibrosis accompanies clusters of atypical cloud-like megakaryocytes and a driver mutation, which the silver stain alone cannot show.
HCL produces a fine, delicate, diffuse reticulin mesh around individual fried-egg lymphoid cells rather than coarse streaming bundles.
